explanation: Even voluntary destitution and dramatic martyrdom are spiritually bankrupt if motivated by pride rather than love. 1 Corinthians 13:3 (KJV) - "And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing."

question: What four positive and negative attributes define the character of charity in 1 Corinthians 13:4?
opt1: Charity is swift to anger, highly critical, jealous of others, and proud
opt2: Charity seeketh vengeance, boasteth of its wealth, and demandeth honor
opt3: Charity flattereth rulers, accumulateth gold, and mocketh the poor
opt4: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up
correct: Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up
explanation: Love is characterized by patient endurance, proactive kindness, freedom from envy, and genuine humility. 1 Corinthians 13:4 (KJV) - "Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,"

question: How does charity behave regarding selfish ambition, temper, and grievances in 1 Corinthians 13:5?
opt1: Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil
opt2: Demands its legal rights aggressively, holds grudges, and seeks revenge
opt3: Keeps a careful record of all insults and retaliates in due season
opt4: Behaves rudely toward inferiors and flatters the powerful
correct: Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil
explanation: Love is courteous, selfless, slow to anger, and keeps no running tally of wrongs suffered. 1 Corinthians 13:5 (KJV) - "Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil;"

question: In what does charity rejoice and what does it refuse to celebrate in 1 Corinthians 13:6?
opt1: Rejoiceth in the secret sins and failures of rival teachers
opt2: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth
opt3: Rejoiceth in flattering lies that preserve peace at any cost
opt4: Rejoiceth when enemies are destroyed by pestilence
correct: Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth
explanation: Love finds no joy in sin or injustice, but celebrates when truth triumphs and flourishes. 1 Corinthians 13:6 (KJV) - "Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth;"

question: What fourfold invincible shield defines charity's tenacity in 1 Corinthians 13:7?
opt1: Resenteth all things, suspecteth all things, feareth all things
opt2: Conquereth all things by force, demandeth all things, boasteth of all things
opt3: Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things
opt4: Exposeth all things to public mockery, despairing of all things
correct: Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things
explanation: Love covers faults patiently, trusts God's best, refuses to abandon hope, and perseveres through all trials. 1 Corinthians 13:7 (KJV) - "Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things."

question: What eternal permanence distinguishes charity from charismatic gifts in 1 Corinthians 13:8?
opt1: Prophecies shall endure for ever, while charity shall pass away
opt2: Tongues are eternal, but charity was given only for the apostolic age
opt3: Knowledge is the supreme virtue that outlasteth all spiritual gifts
opt4: Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away
correct: Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away
explanation: Partial gifts of prophecy, tongues, and knowledge are temporary scaffolding; agape love is eternal. 1 Corinthians 13:8 (KJV) - "Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away."

question: What will happen to partial, imperfect spiritual knowledge when that which is perfect arrives in 1 Corinthians 13:9-10?
opt1: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part. But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away
opt2: Our present partial knowledge shall be inscribed in books of stone
opt3: The apostles shall return to preach in all the synagogues of the earth
opt4: The gift of tongues shall multiply across all the animal creation
correct: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part. But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away
explanation: Our present knowledge and prophecy are piecemeal and partial, destined to be superseded by full consummation. 1 Corinthians 13:9-10 (KJV) - "For we know in part, and we prophesy in part. But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away."

question: Which triad of Christian virtues abides forever, and which is declared the greatest in 1 Corinthians 13:13?
opt1: Wisdom, power, and wealth; and the greatest of these is power
opt2: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity
opt3: Miracles, tongues, and prophecy; and the greatest of these is tongues
opt4: Circumcision, sacrifice, and the Law; and the greatest is the Law
correct: And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity
explanation: Faith and hope find their ultimate consummation in eternity, but love endures forever as the greatest attribute of God Himself. 1 Corinthians 13:13 (KJV) - "And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity."

question: What spiritual gift does Paul specifically urge the church to pursue above tongues in 1 Corinthians 14:1?
opt1: Desire rather that ye may speak in seventy unknown languages
opt2: Desire rather that ye may perform dramatic miracles of fire
opt3: Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy
opt4: Desire rather that ye may amass gold for the building of temples
correct: Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy
explanation: Paul prioritizes prophecy (intelligible divine truth proclaimed) over uninterpreted tongues because it directly edifies the church. 1 Corinthians 14:1 (KJV) - "Follow after charity, and desire spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy."

question: What three vital blessings does the one who prophesieth communicate unto men in 1 Corinthians 14:3?
opt1: He speaketh to condemn, to strike with fear, and to impoverish
opt2: He speaketh in riddles, in dark sayings, and in philosophical doubts
opt3: He speaketh to display his personal wisdom, eloquence, and fame
opt4: He that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort
correct: He that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort
explanation: Biblical prophetic ministry builds up (edification), motivates to godliness (exhortation), and heals the hurting (comfort). 1 Corinthians 14:3 (KJV) - "But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort."

question: How does uninterpreted tongue-speaking contrast with prophecy regarding corporate edification in 1 Corinthians 14:4?
opt1: He that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church
opt2: Both gifts edify the whole congregation equally without interpretation
opt3: Tongues edify the angels, while prophecy edifieth only the speaker
opt4: Prophecy edifieth only the speaker, while tongues convert the heathen
correct: He that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church
explanation: Private tongues may benefit the individual speaker, but intelligible prophecy strengthens the corporate assembly. 1 Corinthians 14:4 (KJV) - "He that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church."

question: What musical instruments does Paul cite to illustrate the necessity of clear, distinct sounds in 1 Corinthians 14:7-8?
opt1: Cymbals and tambourines played in the festival dances
opt2: Pipe or harp... For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?
opt3: Lutes and organs sounding upon the city walls
opt4: Drums beating in the dark forests of Gaul
correct: Pipe or harp... For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?
explanation: Just as indistinct bugle calls confuse an army in battle, unintelligible church speech creates spiritual confusion. 1 Corinthians 14:7-8 (KJV) - "And even things without life giving sound, whether pipe or harp, except they give a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped? For if the trumpet give an uncertain sound, who shall prepare himself to the battle?"

question: What radical preference does Paul declare regarding his speech within the corporate assembly in 1 Corinthians 14:19?
opt1: I had rather speak ten thousand words in ecstatic tongues than five words of doctrine
opt2: I had rather remain silent for ever than teach the unlearned brethren
opt3: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding... than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue
opt4: I had rather recite the poems of Homer than preach the gospel of Christ
correct: Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding... than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue
explanation: Five intelligible, instructional words that edify the church vastly outweigh ten thousand unintelligible ecstatic utterances. 1 Corinthians 14:19 (KJV) - "Yet in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that by my voice I might teach others also, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue."

question: How will an unbeliever or unlearned visitor react when all believers prophesy in 1 Corinthians 14:24-25?
opt1: He will mock the assembly, saying, Ye are all mad and intoxicated
opt2: He will report the congregation to the Roman police for sedition
opt3: He will fall into a deep sleep through boredom and depart quietly
opt4: He is convinced of all, he is judged of all: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship God
correct: He is convinced of all, he is judged of all: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship God
explanation: Clear, penetrating prophetic truth convicts the conscience, unmasks secret sins, and drives the visitor to his knees in repentance. 1 Corinthians 14:24-25 (KJV) - "But if all prophesy, and there come in one that believeth not, or one unlearned, he is convinced of all, he is judged of all: And thus are the secrets of his heart made manifest; and so falling down on his face he will worship God, and report that God is in you of a truth."

question: What strict regulatory limit does Paul place on public tongue-speaking in 1 Corinthians 14:27-28?
opt1: Let it be by two, or at the most by three, and that by course; and let one interpret. But if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church
opt2: Let the entire congregation shout in tongues simultaneously for two hours
opt3: Let tongues be spoken freely without any need of interpretation
opt4: Let only the elders speak in tongues while women interpret
correct: Let it be by two, or at the most by three, and that by course; and let one interpret. But if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church
explanation: Public tongues must be strictly limited to two or three, taken in turn, and silenced immediately if no interpreter is present. 1 Corinthians 14:27-28 (KJV) - "If any man speak in an unknown tongue, let it be by two, or at the most by three, and that by course; and let one interpret. But if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church; and let him speak to himself, and to God."

question: Why are prophets fully capable of exercising self-control during church services in 1 Corinthians 14:32?
opt1: Because an angel physically restrains the tongue of the speaker
opt2: And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets
opt3: Because the civil Roman magistrates enforce total silence
opt4: Because the prophetic trance deprives the speaker of all conscious will
correct: And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets
explanation: Unlike pagan ecstatic frenzy where speakers lose control, true Holy Spirit inspiration leaves the prophet in full self-control. 1 Corinthians 14:32 (KJV) - "And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets."

question: What fundamental theological truth about God's nature establishes liturgical order in 1 Corinthians 14:33?
opt1: For God delighteth in ecstatic chaos and loud shouting in worship
opt2: For God changeth His standards according to the culture of each city
opt3: For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints
opt4: For God is pleased with rival factions contending for dominance
correct: For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints
explanation: Chaotic, disorderly worship misrepresents God, who is the author of harmony, peace, and dignified order. 1 Corinthians 14:33 (KJV) - "For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace, as in all churches of the saints."

question: What famous overarching canon governs all Christian public worship in 1 Corinthians 14:40?
opt1: Let every man do that which is right in his own eyes
opt2: Let all meetings be spontaneous without any leadership or rules
opt3: Let the wealthy members govern all church proceedings
opt4: Let all things be done decently and in order
correct: Let all things be done decently and in order
explanation: The universal rule for Christian gatherings: propriety, decorum, and structural order (kata taxin) must prevail. 1 Corinthians 14:40 (KJV) - "Let all things be done decently and in order."

question: What historical core facts constitute the gospel which Paul delivered 'first of all' in 1 Corinthians 15:3-4?
opt1: That Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures
opt2: That Christ gave us a new moral philosophy to reform the Roman Empire
opt3: That Christ commanded the circumcision of all nations under the law
opt4: That Christ came to establish an earthly monarchy in Jerusalem
correct: That Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures
explanation: The non-negotiable core of the gospel creed: Christ's substitutionary death, burial, and third-day resurrection according to Scripture. 1 Corinthians 15:3-4 (KJV) - "For I delivered unto you first of all that which I also received, how that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures:"

question: To how many brethren at once did the resurrected Christ appear as recorded in 1 Corinthians 15:6?
opt1: Seventy disciples in the upper room
opt2: Above five hundred brethren at once
opt3: The twelve apostles only on the Mount of Olives
opt4: Three thousand converts on the Day of Pentecost
correct: Above five hundred brethren at once
explanation: Over 500 eyewitnesses saw the risen Lord simultaneously, most of whom were still alive to testify when Paul wrote. 1 Corinthians 15:6 (KJV) - "After that, he was seen of above five hundred brethren at once; of whom the greater part remain unto this present, but some are fallen asleep."

question: What catastrophic spiritual consequences would follow if Christ were not literally raised from the dead in 1 Corinthians 15:14, 17?
opt1: Christianity would still remain a lovely moral philosophy of virtue
opt2: Believers would simply reincarnate into future generations on earth
opt3: Then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain... ye are yet in your sins
opt4: The church would simply adopt the ceremonial laws of Aaron
correct: Then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain... ye are yet in your sins
explanation: Without the historical resurrection, apostolic preaching is a lie, faith is futile, and all humanity remains under the guilt of sin. 1 Corinthians 15:14, 17 (KJV) - "And if Christ be not risen, then is our preaching vain, and your faith is also vain. And if Christ be not raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins."

question: What pathetic evaluation applies to Christians if our hope in Christ is limited only to this earthly life in 1 Corinthians 15:19?
opt1: We are still superior to the philosophers of Athens
opt2: We are blessed with earthly peace and long life
opt3: We have attained the highest good of mortal existence
opt4: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable
correct: If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable
explanation: If there is no resurrection, Christians—who sacrifice earthly pleasures and endure persecution—are the most pitiable fools on earth. 1 Corinthians 15:19 (KJV) - "If in this life only we have hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable."

question: As what is the resurrected Christ proclaimed regarding all deceased believers in 1 Corinthians 15:20?
opt1: Now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept
opt2: Christ became an angelic spirit who watches over the dead
opt3: Christ became an earthly prophet whose words inspire morality
opt4: Christ became a symbolic memory in the hearts of His disciples
correct: Now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept
explanation: Christ is the Firstfruits (aparchē)—the guarantee and pledge that the full resurrection harvest of all believers will follow. 1 Corinthians 15:20 (KJV) - "But now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept."

question: What final enemy will be utterly destroyed by Christ before handing the Kingdom to the Father in 1 Corinthians 15:26?
opt1: The empire of Rome and its imperial armies
opt2: The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death
opt3: The pagan philosophies of Greece and Egypt
opt4: The physical oceans and mountains of the earth
correct: The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death
explanation: Death, the ultimate consequence of the Fall, will be totally annihilated at the final resurrection. 1 Corinthians 15:26 (KJV) - "The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death."

question: Which quotation from the Greek poet Menander warns against corrupt companions in 1 Corinthians 15:33?
opt1: Eat, drink, and be merry, for tomorrow we die
opt2: A wise man ruleth over the stars of heaven
opt3: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners
opt4: Virtue is its own sufficient reward upon the earth
correct: Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners
explanation: Paul warns that associating with false teachers who deny the resurrection will inevitably destroy moral character. 1 Corinthians 15:33 (KJV) - "Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners."

question: What four glorious contrasts describe the sowing and raising of the believer's body in 1 Corinthians 15:42-44?
opt1: Sown in wealth, raised in poverty; sown in light, raised in darkness
opt2: Sown as an angel, raised as an earthly king on mount Zion
opt3: Sown in stone, raised in gold; sown in water, raised in fire
opt4: Sown in corruption, raised in incorruption: sown in dishonour, raised in glory: sown in weakness, raised in power: sown a natural body, raised a spiritual body
correct: Sown in corruption, raised in incorruption: sown in dishonour, raised in glory: sown in weakness, raised in power: sown a natural body, raised a spiritual body
explanation: The resurrection body undergoes radical transformation: imperishable, glorious, powerful, and Spirit-animated. 1 Corinthians 15:42-44 (KJV) - "So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption: It is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is a spiritual body."

question: What great prophetic mystery regarding living believers at the final trumpet is revealed in 1 Corinthians 15:51-52?
opt1: We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump
opt2: All living believers shall flee into the desert to escape the plagues
opt3: The righteous shall remain on earth while the wicked are taken into the sky
opt4: Every soul shall be reincarnated into an uncorruptible body in Jerusalem
correct: We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump
explanation: At the last trumpet, living saints will not experience physical death (sleep), but will be instantaneously transformed into immortality. 1 Corinthians 15:51-52 (KJV) - "Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed."

question: What practical pastoral exhortation concludes this great chapter on the resurrection in 1 Corinthians 15:58?
opt1: Therefore, cease all earthly labor and wait passively upon the mountains
opt2: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord
opt3: Therefore, build magnificent stone tombs to preserve your mortal bodies
opt4: Therefore, debate no more with the philosophers concerning the afterlife
correct: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord
explanation: Because the resurrection is certain, Christian service has eternal significance and will never be in vain. 1 Corinthians 15:58 (KJV) - "Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord."

question: On which day of the week were the believers commanded to set aside their charitable contributions in 1 Corinthians 16:2?
opt1: Upon the seventh day of the week at the closing of the Sabbath
opt2: Upon the day of the new moon at the beginning of each month
opt3: Upon the first day of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as God hath prospered him
opt4: Upon the annual feast day of Pentecost in the temple
correct: Upon the first day of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as God hath prospered him
explanation: Systematic, proportionate giving was established on Sunday (the first day of the week), commemorating Christ's resurrection. 1 Corinthians 16:2 (KJV) - "Upon the first day of the week let every one of you lay by him in store, as God hath prospered him, that there be no gatherings when I come."

question: In which city did Paul intend to tarry until Pentecost because a great and effectual door was opened to him in 1 Corinthians 16:8-9?
opt1: Rome
opt2: Athens
opt3: Antioch
opt4: Ephesus (For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and there are many adversaries)
correct: Ephesus (For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and there are many adversaries)
explanation: Paul remained in Ephesus to exploit extraordinary gospel opportunities despite fierce opposition from adversaries. 1 Corinthians 16:8-9 (KJV) - "But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost. For a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and there are many adversaries."

question: What instructions did Paul give regarding the reception of young Timothy in 1 Corinthians 16:10?
opt1: Now if Timotheus come, see that he may be with you without fear: for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also do
opt2: Send him back to Ephesus immediately, for he is too young to instruct you
opt3: Demand letters of commendation from the high priest before hearing him
opt4: Examine his lineage to ensure he is of the tribe of Levi
correct: Now if Timotheus come, see that he may be with you without fear: for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also do
explanation: The Corinthians were instructed to treat Timothy with respect and ensure his safety, honoring his faithful ministry. 1 Corinthians 16:10 (KJV) - "Now if Timotheus come, see that he may be with you without fear: for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also do."

question: Why had Apollos not visited Corinth despite Paul's urgent requests in 1 Corinthians 16:12?
opt1: He was shipwrecked off the coast of Crete and lost his books
opt2: His will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time
opt3: He was imprisoned by the proconsul Gallio in the city of Achaia
opt4: He had vowed never to set foot in Greece again
correct: His will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time
explanation: Apollos exercised independent judgment, deciding not to visit Corinth while partisan factions misused his name. 1 Corinthians 16:12 (KJV) - "As touching our brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren: but his will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time."

question: What fourfold military-like watchwords are commanded in 1 Corinthians 16:13?
opt1: Flee the battle, hide in the caves, surrender your arms, weep bitterly
opt2: Take the sword, overthrow the magistrates, conquer the forum, reign as kings
opt3: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong
opt4: Debate the philosophers, amass worldly wealth, seek earthly fame, be proud
correct: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong
explanation: Paul issues brisk, martial commands: be vigilant, stand firm in doctrine, act courageously like mature men, and be strong. 1 Corinthians 16:13 (KJV) - "Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong."

question: What comprehensive law of love balances the martial vigor of verse 13 in 1 Corinthians 16:14?
opt1: Let all your things be done for personal profit
opt2: Let all your things be done with secret cunning
opt3: Let all your things be done with fierce retaliation
opt4: Let all your things be done with charity
correct: Let all your things be done with charity
explanation: Strength and courage must always be governed by agape love; without love, strength degenerates into brutality. 1 Corinthians 16:14 (KJV) - "Let all your things be done with charity."

question: To what holy calling had the household of Stephanas, the firstfruits of Achaia, devoted themselves in 1 Corinthians 16:15?
opt1: They have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints
opt2: They had purchased the public baths of Corinth for the church
opt3: They had trained an armed guard to escort the apostles
opt4: They had opened a philosophical academy near the harbor
correct: They have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints
explanation: Stephanas' family devoted themselves with passionate zeal (addicted themselves) to practical Christian service and hospitality. 1 Corinthians 16:15 (KJV) - "I beseech you, brethren, (ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have addicted themselves to the ministry of the saints,)"

question: Which prominent tentmaking couple sent hearty greetings with the church in their house in 1 Corinthians 16:19?
opt1: Ananias and Sapphira
opt2: Aquila and Priscilla
opt3: Zacharias and Elisabeth
opt4: Philemon and Apphia
correct: Aquila and Priscilla
explanation: Aquila and Priscilla, residing in Ephesus, hosted a vibrant house church and sent warm Christian greetings. 1 Corinthians 16:19 (KJV) - "The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Priscilla salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house."

question: What solemn Aramaic watchword and curse does Paul pronounce in his own handwriting in 1 Corinthians 16:22?
opt1: Peace be upon the twelve tribes of Israel, Amen Selah
opt2: Glory to Caesar Augustus throughout all the earth, Pax Romana
opt3: If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maran-atha
opt4: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of Sabaoth, Hosanna in the highest
correct: If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maran-atha
explanation: Those who do not love the Lord Jesus are accursed (Anathema); Maran-atha cries 'Our Lord, come!' 1 Corinthians 16:22 (KJV) - "If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema Maranatha."

question: With what tender benediction does Paul conclude this momentous epistle in 1 Corinthians 16:23-24?
opt1: The curse of the Law be upon all who disobey this epistle, Amen
opt2: Tribute and taxes be paid unto the magistrates without complaint, Amen
opt3: May the angels preserve you from the plagues of the Gentiles, Amen
opt4: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen
correct: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen
explanation: Paul concludes with the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and an embrace of personal pastoral love for the entire church. 1 Corinthians 16:23-24 (KJV) - "The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen."
